policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'thine enemy' is singular; the qere אֹיִבְךָ is singular 'thine enemy', while the ketiv איביך reads as plural 'thine enemies'. The English number settles it for the qere.

Qere מֵהַמְּעָרָה and ketiv מן המערה both mean 'out of the cave'; the difference is the prefixed vs. separate preposition. ASV 'went out of the cave' renders either identically and carries no mapped textual note. Base fallback retained.

Qere וְאַתָּה and ketiv ואת are both the 2nd-person pronoun 'and thou' (the ketiv a defective spelling); ASV 'And thou hast declared' renders either identically and has no mapped textual note. Base fallback retained.
